senses.gloss: (freq. פִּיטּוּם, פִּיטָּם) c. (פטס to expand, cmp. פָּטַם 2)
a large cylindrical vessel, cask or tub of earthen material (corresp. to πίθος, a. to dolium; v. Sm. Ant.3 Engl. ed., s. v. Dolium).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:12">B. Mets. IV, 12</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 60a:4">60ᵃ</cite>) <he>התגר … פיטם אחד</he> (Bab. ed. <cite ref="Q00616"><he>פיטום</he></cite>; Y. ed. Ven. a. Mish. ed. Nap. <he>פיטס</he>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 400) a merchant may buy wine from several presses and put it into one cask.

<cite ref="Ketubot 111b">Keth. 111ᵇ</cite> in the days to come <he>מביא ענבה … כפ׳ גדול</he> one will bring in one cluster of grapes on a wagon or in a boat and place it in a corner of his house, and take his supply of wine from it, as if it were a large jar; <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 317:7">Sifré Deut. 317</cite> <he>כשותה מן הפיטום</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 944">Yalk. ib. 944</cite> <he>ומסתפק והולך מן הפטים</he> (read <he>כמן הפ׳</he>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 160:1">Yalk. Gen. 160</cite> <he>בפ׳ גדול</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 3:7">R. Hash. III, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 27b">27ᵇ</cite>) <he>הפיטם</he> (Bab. ed. <he>הפיטס</he>; Ms. M. <he>הפיטם</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).
Tosef. Ohol. X, 3 פ׳ שהוא עומד וכ׳ a piṭṭus (pithos) standing in a room and reaching from the floor to the ceiling.

<cite ref="Tosefta Kelim Kamma 4:16">Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. IV, 16</cite> <he>פיטים שקירו וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.) a large tub to which one made a cover to use it as a stove, and which he plastered over with clay.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 3:1:3">Y. Bets. III, 62ᵃ</cite> top <he>צד הוא בפיטס</he> he may catch an animal (on the Holy Day) by chasing it into a tub; Y. Sabb. III, 14ᵃ bot. <he>בפיתם</he> (read <he>ס …</he>).
<cite ref="Tosefta Tevul Yom 2:3">Tosef. T’bul Yom II, 3</cite> <cite ref="Q00897"><he>פִּיתוֹס</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>פִּיטְּסִין</he>, <cite ref="Q00616"><he>פִּטְּ׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 3:6">Kel. III, 6</cite> <he>שטופלין בה הפ׳</he> (Ar. <he>הפדיסין</he>) wherewith they line the tubs.
<cite ref="Beitzah 15b:10">Bets. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>הללו בעלי פ׳</he> those (the first to leave the lecture room) are owners of tubs of wine, contrad. to <cite ref="H00080"><he>חבית</he></cite> &c.

senses.gloss: a vessel made of brittle clay and requiring lining.—Pl. פִּיטְּסוֹת.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 6:2">B. Bath. VI, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Batra 93b:14">93ᵇ</cite>) <he>קנקנים בשרון … פיטסות למאה</he> (Ms. H. a. R. <cite ref="Q00196"><he>פּוֹטְסוֹת</he></cite>; Mish. ed. <he>פִּיטַסְיָאוֹת</he>, Y. ed. <he>פִּיטְסָאוֹת</he>) if a man buys jugs (<he>קנקנים</he>) in Sharon, he must accept ten thin jugs for every hundred; ib. 97ᵇ, expl. <he>נאות ומגופרות</he>, v. <cite ref="N00004"><he>נָא</he> II</cite>; Tosef. ib. VI, 3, sq. <cite ref="Q00196"><he>פוטסות</he></cite> ed. Zuck. (oth. ed. <he>פוניסות</he>, <cite ref="Q00725"><he>פינוסות</he></cite>, corr. acc.).
